title: Cloud saved-scan mutations can report success without an authoritative mutation
sourceEquivalence: services/savedScansCloud.ts is unchanged between the authoritative mobile and tested promotion source
environment: Real Staging PostgREST through actual Supabase JS SDK; synthetic cached-session provider; two tagged synthetic accounts cleaned
observed: Re-save of own tombstone returned ok:true while the authoritative row remained deleted
Soft-delete targeting another synthetic account's scan returned ok:true while the foreign row correctly remained active
Fresh own scan save returned ok:true and the authoritative inserted row existed
rootCause: Existing RLS UPDATE policy excludes tombstones, although explicit save attempts to clear deleted_at. Existing-row save and soft-delete inspect only error; PostgREST zero-row filtered updates have no error and were represented as successful.
impact: Re-saved scans do not return in cloud history and denied/stale mutations may display success. No cross-account read/write or paid-provider dispatch demonstrated.
repairPlan: Permit explicit own scan restoration under current active-account authority; require returned matching row acknowledgment before existing-row save or soft-delete success. Preserve foreign-owner refusal and no client hard-delete policy.
status: CLOSED — SOURCE REPAIRED / MERGED / CI VERIFIED; runtime migration application separately governed
reverification: Before actual service+Staging:2contract failures of1defect, fresh-save positive and2cleanups. After client source:5PASS. Actual Postgres-engine SQL proves restoration after migration.
